publisher: NFL.com (official NFL publisher) and NFL club sites

sources.title: Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season
sources.used_for: Availability: practice status and game status per listed player; current-state only
sources.verified_by: read line by line; the sample rows on the Flagged page are quoted verbatim
sources.evidence: Per-matchup tables with columns Player / Position / Injuries / Practice Status / Game Status. Many rows carry a practice status with a blank Game Status; blank cells are published as blank. This page is a current-state page, not a dated archive: it cannot by itself support a point-in-time backtest.

The international block names 'Mexico City' for Vikings at 49ers, which is the only neutral-site fixture of the week. Bye list: ATL, CLE, GB, LA, NE, SEA.

sources.evidence: One Week 10 game is already final (Commanders 24, Giants 21, Thursday 12 November); the remainder are listed as scheduled fixtures on the same day, 15 November, with kickoff times. The Munich block names the international game Patriots at Lions.

blocked.what: Official market prices (closing lines, moneylines, totals) for 2026 games
blocked.detail: NFL.com pages fetched here publish results and schedules, not historical prices. No licensed price archive is available to this session. The origination board therefore publishes our own number with the market column blank and flag OV-F02. No backtest ROI, closing-line value or vig decomposition is published.

The nfl.com depth-chart route 404s (OV-S14). Club depth pages are owned by other sessions' captures and were not re-fetched by this session. No depth rank, starter/backup label or replacement order is asserted in this workspace.

blocked.what: Official snap counts and inactive lists
blocked.detail: The tested league snap-count route 404s (OV-S15). Snap share and inactive lists are therefore absent; the workspace does not infer them.
The injury report page is a current-state page. One capture cannot be replayed, so no availability feature is used in any model published here.
